correctness.rationale: The recurrence, including n=1, is (2 delta-1)*kappa_1=id. Its coefficientwise absolutely convergent expansion yields the shifted-prime product with weight 2^(-r-1), including the r=0 term. For z comparable to sqrt(x), effective PNT and partial summation give the difference of log logs; the scaled kernels after removing the prime harmonic contribution have integrals 1 and 0. In the small-p tail one may split at sqrt(z): the cruder O(sqrt(z) log z) bound below it is negligible and dyadic groups above it give O(epsilon(1+|log epsilon|) z/log z) for the logarithmic kernel. The large-p dyadic tail is O(z/(M log z)) for both kernels. The errors are uniform on compact z/sqrt(x) intervals. The derivative signs and strict concavity trap the real saddle at (1+o(1))sqrt(x); rounding inside the same interval is harmless. Beyond 2sqrt(x) the negative slope gives a geometric tail of size O(log x) times the peak term, and the rest has O(sqrt(x)) terms. Thus taking a log incurs only O(log x), negligible at the claimed scale. Independent bounded replay: python -B /workspace/checks/bounded.py compares the full divisor recursion to exact rational series enclosures through the fifth primorial; it does not certify the asymptotic. Passage from prime endpoints to all real cutoffs is included in the uniform PNT proof.
